newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks drop, react to economic emergency.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks drop, react to economic emergency.

text.p: Colombian stocks fell for the fifth consecutive session as investors showed signs of nervousness over the effects of the state of economic emergency, now in its second week.
Bogota's IBB index dropped 1.94 percent to 986.56 amid a 3 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED index dived 2.12 percent to 15,717.47 amid a 2.5 billion peso volume.
Both exchanges had climbed about 25 percent in the first sessions of 1997.
"Such rapid rises are dangerous because the falls also tend to be dramatic," one Bogota broker said.
Taking into account recent falls, Bogota is still up 16.9 percent on the start of the year and Medellin is up 17 percent -- better than they performed in the whole of last year.
"We're seeing profit-taking as a reaction to the economic emergency and the ridiculous sentences handed down to the Rodriguez Orejuela brothers," another broker said.

President Ernesto Samper declared an economic emergency at the start of last week in a bid to rein in Colombia's yawning fiscal deficit. The crisis measures so far announced include new laws to stem the influx of foreign investment, broaden the tax base and slash back public spending.

Coupled with the emergency is the renewed tension in U.S.- Colombian relations, sparked by the jail terms handed down last Friday by a regional judge to the Rodrguezes, who headed the mighty Cali drug cartel for more than 20 years.
Lightweight sentences, with maximum reductions for confessions, will see them free in just five years.

More importantly for investors, the outcry caused by the sentences has revived the specter that the United States will not only decertify Colombia as an ally in the drug war for the second year running, but could also impose tough economic sanctions to punish exports.
The biggest losers in Bogota were Bancoquia bank, down 4.36 percent to 2,630 and brewing giant Bavaria, down 3.74 percent to 5,680.
"We thought we'd seen the last of the profit-taking yesterday, but economic and political factors appear to be driving down the markets," the broker added.
In Medellin, supermarket chain Cadenalco dived 5.67 percent to 849, cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe dropped 5.66 percent to 5,000 and Banco Ganadero ordinary shares lost 5 percent, down to 285.

"These three shares are now back to more or less the same levels at which they started the year. Cadenalco has clearly been hit by the economic emergency and the tax to be imposed on debit card payments," a Medellin broker said.
Bavaria dropped 4.24 percent to 5,650 while cigarrette manufacturer Coltabaco lost 3.14 percent, falling to 3,700.
